headline: Fungi are neither plants nor animals—they're a separate kingdom with their own strange biology
universal_truth: What seems similar may be deeply different; surface appearances can deceive
fun_facts: Fungi are more closely related to animals than to plants
The largest organism on Earth is a honey fungus in Oregon—covering 2,385 acres underground
Fungi can't make their own food; they digest things externally and absorb the nutrients
discussion_questions: Why did we used to think fungi were plants?
What role do fungi play in ecosystems?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Mushrooms look like plants—they grow from the ground, they don't move. But fungi aren't plants. They don't photosynthesize; they digest like animals. Genetically, you're more closely related to a mushroom than a mushroom is to any plant.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: If fungi can't make food like plants and can't eat like animals, how do they survive? What unique strategy does this hidden kingdom use to get nutrition?
cliff.prompt: How do fungi get their food?

options.text: They release digestive enzymes externally, breaking down material around them, then absorb the nutrients
options.response: Yes. Fungi digest outside their bodies—releasing enzymes that break down dead matter, then absorbing the results. It's like eating in reverse.

options.text: They absorb nutrients directly from soil like plant roots
options.response: They do absorb, but first they must break down complex materials with enzymes...

q1.title: Third Kingdom
q1.script: For centuries, fungi were classified as plants. DNA revealed the truth: fungi are a separate kingdom, more closely related to animals. They split from animals about a billion years ago. Plants are more distant relatives.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Third Kingdom"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Hidden Giants
q2.script: What you see as a mushroom is just the fruiting body—the reproductive part. Underground, networks of fungal threads can spread for miles. The largest known organism is a honey fungus covering over 2,000 acres in Oregon.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Essential Recyclers
q3.script: Fungi decompose dead matter, returning nutrients to the soil. Without fungi, dead plants and animals would pile up, nutrients locked away. Fungi are nature's recyclers—essential for ecosystems to function.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: What seems similar may be deeply different. Fungi teach that surface appearances deceive. Understanding the hidden reality—the underground network, the unique biology—reveals what matters.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 148. Tomorrow, we'll explore tiny life everywhere—microorganisms. Until then, remember: you're more closely related to that mushroom than it is to any plant.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Hidden Connections - Look Beneath the Surface
growTrack.activity: Find two things that seem similar but are deeply different—or two things that seem different but are closely related. Fungi looked like plants but aren't. What in your life might be misclassified by surface appearance?
